paper_title: Audio-Visual Efficient Conformer for Robust Speech Recognition
caption: Audio-only back-end modules FLOPs (Billion).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the computational cost, measured in Giga FLOPs (billions of floating-point operations), of different modules within the audio back-end Conformer stages of a speech recognition model. The horizontal axis represents three stages of the Conformer: Stage 1 (d=180, n=500), Stage 2 (d=256, n=250), and Stage 3 (d=360, n=125), where d denotes the dimension and n the number of heads or similar parameters. The vertical axis, labeled "Module Giga FLOPs," ranges from 0 to 0.3 in increments of 0.1, using a linear scale. For each stage, four grouped bars represent different modules: blue for "attention," red for "grouped attention (g=3)," yellow for "patch attention (k=3)," and green for "feed-forward." In Stage 1, the attention module (blue) has the highest FLOPs, approximately 0.28, followed by feed-forward (green) at ~0.12, grouped attention (red) at ~0.15, and patch attention (yellow) at ~0.10. In Stage 2, attention drops to ~0.16, feed-forward remains at ~0.12, grouped attention at ~0.11, and patch attention at ~0.10. In Stage 3, attention further decreases to ~0.12, feed-forward stays at ~0.12, grouped attention at ~0.10, and patch attention at ~0.10. The bars are arranged in the same order across all stages, with no visual emphasis or annotations, and the chart shows a general trend of decreasing computational cost for the attention module across stages, while feed-forward and patch attention remain relatively stable.
